# atuin 18.24.8

## Install atuin 18.24.8

### Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/atuinsh/atuin/releases/download/v18.24.8/atuin-installer.sh | sh
```

### Install prebuilt binaries via powershell script

```sh
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://github.com/atuinsh/atuin/releases/download/v18.24.8/atuin-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

## Verifying GitHub Artifact Attestations

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify):
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --repo atuinsh/atuin
```

You can also download the attestation from [GitHub](https://github.com/atuinsh/atuin/attestations) and verify against that directly:
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --bundle <file-path of downloaded attestation>
```

detail.readme:
making your terminal magical

Atuin gives you, and your agents, a history of everything that happened in your terminal. **Shell history** Atuin replaces your shell history with a SQLite database that records exit codes, working directories, hosts and durations. Hit Ctrlr and find any command you've ever run, on any machine. **Agent Threads** Atuin captures your Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other agent sessions. Start a thread on your laptop, then `atuin resume` it on a different machine, in a different harness. Your agents can, optionally, search everything that's ever happened through the built-in MCP server. Atuin can also sync both history and threads across all of your machines, end-to-end encrypted. Or it can work totally offline! # Quick Start ```bash curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://setup.atuin.sh | sh ``` Then, **restart your shell**. ## History Atuin captures everything you do in the terminal, storing it into a SQLite database. Hitting CTRLr opens a pretty pane with all your bash history. Atuin logs your _exit codes_, _working directories_, _hostnames_, _command duration_ and much much more. You can hit Return to execute a command, Tab to edit any highlighted command.

Agents can search your history too:

As well as the search UI, `atuin` has a CLI interface for searching commands: ```bash # search for all successful `make` commands, recorded after 3pm yesterday atuin search --exit 0 --after "yesterday 3pm" make ``` ## Threads Atuin captures what your agents do. Automatically move your context and thread history from one machine to another, or from one harness to another. With _Atuin Threads_, your agent has access to your full history, and the built-in Atuin MCP gives your agent context on everything you've ever done.

You can take a session you started on your personal computer in Claude Code, and `$ atuin resume` it in a remote machine inside Codex.

Similarly to the _history_ index, you can search through your _threads_: ```bash atuin threads search 'c++' ``` ## Sync Atuin syncs all your AI threads, your shell sessions across all your computers (even ephemeral VMs!). You can either use the official [Atuin Service](https://atuin.sh) or you can self-host the sync server. **Everything it syncs is end-to-end encrypted.** ## Atuin supports [ `zsh`](https://www.zsh.org/), [ `bash`](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/), [ `fish`](https://fishshell.com/), [ `nushell`](https://www.nushell.sh/), [ `xonsh`](https://xon.sh/) and [ `PowerShell`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/) as well as [ `Claude Code`](https://claude.com/product/claude-code), [ `Codex`](https://openai.com/codex/), [ Opencode](https://opencode.ai/), [ Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot), [ Grok](https://x.ai/build), [ Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/), and many more. Atuin does so much more and we have [extensive documentation](https://docs.atuin.sh/)! If you ever need help, reach out to us through our [communities](#community). ## Related projects * [Catpuccin for Atuin](https://github.com/catppuccin/atuin) * [eshell-atuin](https://github.com/SqrtMinusOne/eshell-atuin) * [mob (tiny creatures in your terminal)](https://github.com/bboynton97/mob) Please open a PR for any others! # Community
